'''Plugin and Tool Awareness''' is the rule that agent tools come from plugins
whose state can change at runtime, so the registry must be checked and never
assumed. Absence of a tool from the current toolset usually means its plugin is
'''disabled''', not that the tool was removed or that docs naming it are stale.

== Check the registry ==

* Agent tools are provided by plugins of type tool, platform or provider; each
  can be enabled, disabled or not found.
* The registry is reachable through the plugin manager list tool or through
  <code>GET /api/plugins</code>; see [[Omniagent API]] for the route map.
* Enable a disabled plugin at
  <code>POST /api/plugins/tools/&lt;source&gt;/&lt;name&gt;/enable</code> and
  disable it at the matching <code>/disable</code> route. Use the registry source
  field to pick the URL segment (built-in, bundled or remote).

{{OmniFact
|what=runtime plugin and tool registry awareness
|where=the omniagent plugin registry
|status=standing rule
|source=Reference/Omniagent/Plugin-Tool-Awareness.md
}}

== Filesystem plugin ==

The built-in filesystem plugin exposes read, write, list, search and info tools.
Reads are unrestricted; writes are sandboxed to the workspace directory plus the
configured data, profiles and plugins subdirectories. The configuration file is
not agent-writable. The plugin history is a cautionary tale: it was disabled
after a wedge caused by synchronous filesystem handlers on async workers, the
root cause was fixed in core, and the plugin was re-enabled on the live registry.
Do NOT run a recursive glob search from the filesystem root: it wedges the
server.

== Tool priority ==

Purpose-built beats generic: use the filesystem plugin for file operations, the
search and database tools for discovery, and docker or compose only to run code
and builds. Shelling out to a container for grep, listdir or cat is a known waste
and more privileged than needed.

== Role separation ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Role !! Owns
|-
| Executor || Implementation plus minimal relevant evidence: compile or build, lint, the single most relevant test. No full verification batteries.
|-
| Tester || Verification: the full relevant suites, real run output and the PASS gate. An executor's minimal run never replaces the tester's own run.
|}

== Naming and delegation rules ==

* Tool names are runtime-qualified as <code>{plugin}__{tool}</code> and must
  match what the plugin ACTUALLY registers. Never call a plugin a tool, and note
  that a plugin can be installed under another name, so only the qualified runtime
  name is stable.
* Core setting text must be consumer-agnostic: it must not name a specific
  stack's hooks or dashboard.
* A setting whose only job is to tell the agent WHICH tool to use must NOT exist.
  As long as the tool is enabled and the profile is permitted, the instruction
  belongs in the template, skill or wiki.
* A real credential in a header stays a secret reference, never a literal value;
  see [[Secrets Store]].
* Provider-specific response quirks are delegated to a tool behind an
  empty-by-default setting, following the same shape as [[Redaction]], instead of
  branching on the provider inside core.

== Drift guard ==

The registry default for the git-sync setting must equal the registered tool name,
and the check computes the qualified name from the plugin manifest at test time
rather than comparing against a hard-coded literal. A live gate confirms
<code>GET /settings</code> returns the qualified value.
